purpose: Fixes issue #300 (api-data-fetching audit findings) by preventing duplicate audit-issue creation with a fail-closed existing-issue search, reconstructing deep/old review-comment threads via a single-pass paginated walk with a direct-fetch fallback, expanding conversation comment windows, keying the lessons cache by the file-path set, propagating failedBatches into results with a 'Partial review' banner, adding an authenticated opencode release lookup with an anonymous fallback, honoring sort direction in the GitLab adapter, and plumbing AbortSignal through the API helpers.
riskRationale: All previously flagged critical/important defects from the first commit (thread duplication, silent audit drop, GitLab ordering, opencode token handling, failedBatches lost on dedup) are fixed and covered by regression tests, and tests/typecheck/lint pass on the final state. Remaining risk is bounded to four important items: missing in_reply_to_id cycle guards in the new GitHub thread-walk loops (hang risk on malformed data), the missing-ancestor walk re-fetching in-window comments sequentially at the window boundary, an ascending issue-comment window that drops preceding context on PRs with more than 500 comments, and a fail-closed audit path that discards already-gathered findings on a transient search failure — none break the primary flows but should be addressed before merge.

text: A well-structured reliability-hardening pass that fixes a genuine stale-lessons-cache bug, prevents duplicate audit issues with a fail-closed existing-issue search, surfaces partial reviews via failedBatches, reconstructs deep comment threads with a single-pass paginated walk plus a direct-fetch fallback, and hardens pagination/abort handling across both adapters. Commit 2 (autofix iteration 1) resolved nearly every finding from the first review with targeted regression tests, and tests/typecheck/lint all pass. Remaining gaps are the adapter-level in_reply_to_id walks lacking the cycle guard conversation.ts added, the missing-ancestor fallback re-fetching in-window comments, the oldest-first issue-comment window losing context on busy PRs, and the audit search hard-failing the whole run on a transient error.

reasoning: Four important items should be addressed before merge: (1) GitHubHelper.getReviewCommentThread's in_reply_to_id walk loops can loop forever on cyclic/malformed API data, hanging the reply webhook; (2) gatherReviewCommentThread's missing-chain fallback re-fetches in-window ancestors instead of resolving them from the in-memory map; (3) gatherIssueCommentThread's ascending window drops all preceding context on PRs with more than 500 issue comments; (4) action/src/audit.ts discards all findings when the existing-issue search fails transiently. Each fix is small, localized, and pattern-matched by the commit-2 tests for sibling logic, so an automated agent can address them reliably.

message: Keying the lessons cache by the sorted, deduplicated file-path set is a correct bug fix: previously lessons for one file set were silently reused for any other file set within the 60s TTL, serving mismatched learning context. It also aligns the lessons cache with the existing mcpDocsCache keying pattern.

failedBatches is propagated into the final result and survives the linter-dedup rebuild branch via the conditional spread (engine.ts:511), and review-body.ts renders it as a prominent 'Partial review' banner — consumers and the autofix loop can now tell findings may be incomplete instead of silently trusting a partial result. The regression test in lib/tests/engine.test.ts guards the dedup-overwrite case.

Reconstructing the review-comment thread from a single paginated list converts an inherently sequential N+1 direct-fetch walk into one bounded fetch. Starting the needsDirectWalk fallback from chainIds[0] (the deepest already-found ancestor) is correct — in-window comments are never re-fetched or re-added — and the regression test explicitly guards against the [1,2,2,3] duplicate-ID bug the first commit produced.

The in_reply_to_id chain walk now indexes comments into a Map for O(1) lookups, guards against cyclic chains with a visited set, direct-fetches missing ancestors/triggers outside the window, and expands the thread to the full subtree (sibling branches preserved). This directly addresses the previous review's O(n*m) walk, hang-on-cycle, and dropped-context findings, all covered by new unit tests including the cyclic-chain case.

GitLabAdapter.paginate now appends order_by=created_at&sort when direction is supplied, fixing the cross-platform ordering mismatch where the 'asc' assumptions in conversation.ts and the thread reconstruction were silently reversed on GitLab (which returns notes newest-first by default). Covered by new ascending/descending paginate tests.

The authenticated release lookup degrades gracefully: the ambient token is used for the first attempt and, on 401/403/404, the request is retried anonymously, so the GitLab CI path (a non-GitHub token sent to api.github.com) fails fast and recovers without aborting setup.

The existing-issue search is now fail-loud: on a pagination failure the action surfaces core.setFailed with a clear message and aborts issue creation rather than silently creating a duplicate audit issue (the bug #300 reported). The audit.integration.test.ts suite verifies the abort and the update-instead-of-duplicate paths.
Fail-fast on comment-fetch errors with a sanitized setFailed message prevents silently miscounted iteration counts that could bypass maxIterations and cause unbounded autofix loops.

None of the in_reply_to_id walk loops in GitHubHelper.getReviewCommentThread — the in-window chain walk (github.ts:906-914), the needsDirectWalk ancestor walk (github.ts:928-933), and walkChainById (github.ts:1011-1016) — guard against cycles. If in_reply_to_id is malformed or cyclic (A→B→A), the walk unshifts the same IDs forever, growing chainIds unboundedly and issuing an unbounded sequence of direct API fetches, hanging the reply webhook (reply.ts:35 calls this with no timeout). This exact malformed-data risk is acknowledged and guarded with a visited set in conversation.ts:191 ('in_reply_to_id comes from external API data and may be malformed'), so the adapter-level implementation should match for consistency.
suggestion: Track visited IDs in each walk loop and break when an id is revisited, mirroring the guard already added in conversation.ts.

message: The missing-chain direct-fetch fallback in gatherReviewCommentThread does not stop at the window boundary: once it reaches an ancestor already present in byId (an in-window comment above the first missing id), it keeps issuing sequential getReviewComment calls for the entire remaining chain instead of resolving them from the in-memory map. When a thread's reply chain straddles the 500-comment window, every in-window ancestor is re-fetched with one API call each — the exact N+1 behavior github.ts's chainIds[0] fix was added to avoid.
suggestion: Resolve in-window ancestors from byId without fetching: check byId.has(ancestorId) (or get) before the direct fetch and only call getReviewComment when the comment is genuinely outside the window, then continue ascending via the known comment's in_reply_to_id.

message: gatherIssueCommentThread fetches the issue-comment window oldest-first (direction 'asc', perPage 100, maxPages 5 = the OLDEST 500 comments). The trigger is a freshly-posted comment, so on any PR with more than 500 issue comments it is never in the window: triggerIdx is always -1, the by-id fallback returns only [triggerComment], and the preceding-5-comments context the previous implementation provided is silently lost on exactly the busiest PRs — contradicting the PR's stated goal of more complete conversation context. The JSDoc note ('older than the window') only makes sense for a newest-first window, confirming the direction is inconsistent with the intent. (The review-comment window in github.ts:891 has the same asc-window perf characteristic, though its ancestor-walk fallback is correct.)
suggestion: Fetch the issue-comment window newest-first (direction 'desc') so the recent trigger is always in-window with its preceding comments, reverse the slice to restore chronological order, and keep the by-id fallback for the now genuinely rare older-than-window case.

message: The fail-closed existing-issue search has a data-loss tradeoff: on a transient search failure (gh.paginate throws after the API already retried 3x), the catch calls core.setFailed and returns, discarding all audit findings — including the issueBody that was already built. For a long-running LLM audit a rate-limit or flaky page fetch becomes full data loss (no issue, no comment) rather than a retry or a degraded write, while the previous behavior at least posted the findings (with a rare duplicate risk).
suggestion: On search failure, retry with backoff (reuse withRetry) before failing closed; as a fallback, log a warning and create the issue without deduplication (accepting a rare duplicate) so findings are never silently lost. Only setFailed if even that fallback fails.

message: The new signal?: AbortSignal parameters on GitHubHelper.api (github.ts:100), GitHubHelper.graphql (github.ts:1435), and GitLabAdapter.api (gitlab-adapter.ts:54) are never passed by any caller — every api()/graphql() invocation omits the argument. The internal abort wiring (listeners, cleanup, withRetry signal) is correct but exercises only dead paths, and handleConversation only checks signal?.aborted (conversation.ts:96) without threading the signal into the API helpers, so the plumbing adds maintenance surface (and a subtle failure mode) with no consumer.
suggestion: Either thread a real signal from the callers that need cancellation (e.g. webhook handlers with request-lifecycle timeouts — conversation.ts already receives a signal parameter), or defer the parameter until a consumer exists.

message: getReviewComment does not surface diff_hunk: its return type (github.ts:826-843) includes id/body/user/path/line/in_reply_to_id but not diff_hunk, even though the GitHub API returns it on GET /pulls/comments/{id}, and the GitLab counterpart (ReviewCommentDetail) has no diff_hunk field either. Consequently in conversation.ts:255 chain.find((c) => c.diff_hunk)?.diff_hunk is undefined whenever the entire ancestor chain was direct-fetched (i.e. the trigger is older than the window) — exactly the deep/old-thread case this PR is meant to support — so the model loses hunk context for older-thread replies.
suggestion: Add diff_hunk?: string to getReviewComment's return type on GitHubHelper (and align the GitLab adapter), then set diffHunk from the first chain comment carrying it so the direct-fetch fallback preserves hunk context.

message: The authenticated release lookup sends the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN / INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN to api.github.com for a public cross-repo endpoint where anonymous access works. Because 403 is in fetchWithRetry's retryableStatuses (opencode.ts:88), a rejected repo-scoped token burns three backoff retries (~7-10s) before the anonymous fallback fires, and the token is transmitted to an endpoint that cannot authorize a cross-repo lookup (least-privilege concern).
suggestion: Drop 403 from the retryable statuses for the authenticated attempt (or add an option) so the deterministic rejection fails fast into the anonymous fallback, and only attach the Authorization header when the token is known to be GitHub-scoped.

message: The abort wiring has a narrow race: signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true }) never fires if the signal is already aborted, so if the caller's signal aborts in the gap between withRetry's top-of-loop signal?.aborted check (retry.ts:85) and this addEventListener, the retried attempt issues a full up-to-30s un-cancellable request. The window is microseconds, so it is unlikely, but it defeats the new cancellation intent.
suggestion: Guard the listener registration with the current aborted state: if (signal?.aborted) controller.abort(); else signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true }); — in both api() and graphql().

message: filePath is derived only from chain[0]?.path (the root), with no fallback, while the adjacent diffHunk uses chain.find((c) => c.diff_hunk) which searches the whole chain. If the root comment is a thread-level comment without a path but the trigger carries one, filePath becomes undefined and the model loses file context. The github.ts version of this logic explicitly falls back to the first chain comment carrying the field (github.ts:961-963, 972); conversation.ts should match.
suggestion: Use the first chain comment carrying a path so file context is preserved when the root lacks a path.

message: Any error in thread gathering (including a single deleted/404 ancestor during the new direct-fetch fallback) is swallowed and the whole conversation is skipped with { thread: [] } (conversation.ts:268-273), so the failure surface grew with the new direct-fetch path while the fallback behavior still drops the entire conversation rather than returning partial context.
suggestion: Return any successfully gathered partial chain with a warning instead of an empty thread when only some ancestor fetches fail, so the model still receives available context.

message: getReviewThreads no longer double-retries (the redundant outer retry-once was removed), which is an improvement, but on a final page failure the loop still breaks and all remaining thread pages are dropped; the comment claims the data is 'marked as partial' (github.ts:1596), yet nothing beyond a warning marks it. getBotReviewThreads/getOpenHumanThreads consequently operate on truncated thread data (e.g. missing open threads) with no way for callers to detect the incompleteness.
suggestion: Track a partial flag on the returned thread data (or rethrow when completeness is required) so consumers of getBotReviewThreads/getOpenHumanThreads know the result may omit threads, rather than relying on an easily-missed warning.

message: The subtree BFS (conversation.ts:237-248) only scans the bounded window (rawComments): sibling and nested replies that fall outside the 500-comment window are silently omitted, since only the ancestor chain is recovered by the by-id fallback. On large PRs the returned thread can therefore miss valid sibling turns, which conflicts with the intent that the conversation is never silently skipped (that guarantee holds only for the ancestor chain).
suggestion: Document the bounded-window limitation explicitly, or extend the direct-fetch fallback to also recover sibling comments by ID when their parent is in the chain but they are outside the window.
